input: Photograph every room for a home inventory record

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether 'every room' includes storage areas, garage, basement, outdoor spaces, and whether individual items need close-up shots versus wide room shots changes the shooting plan entirely.
Whether this is for the user alone, a landlord, an insurance company, or a shared household affects the level of formality, detail, and sign-off required.
The purpose (insurance claim prep, moving out, estate planning, rental handover) determines what must be captured and how formally it needs to be documented.
A hard deadline (e.g., before moving day, before a policy renewal) affects how the task should be scheduled and whether it needs to be done in one session.
The tool used — smartphone, DSLR, a dedicated inventory app — shapes the workflow, file organization, and how photos are stored or shared afterward.
Whether the output needs to be a simple photo album, a labeled spreadsheet with photos, a PDF report, or an upload to an insurance portal defines what 'done' actually looks like.
Whether the user wants to capture serial numbers, receipts, and item values alongside photos — or just visual proof of condition — changes the depth of effort per room.

gold.taskTitle: Photograph every room for home inventory
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to systematically photograph all rooms in their home to create a visual inventory record, likely for insurance, moving, or personal documentation purposes.

questions.title: Which spaces beyond main rooms should be included?
questions.description: Clarify whether the inventory should cover storage areas, garage, basement, attic, outdoor spaces, or only the main living rooms.

questions.title: Who is the intended audience for this record?
questions.description: Determine whether the photos are for personal reference, an insurance provider, a landlord, an estate, or another specific party.

questions.title: What is the primary purpose driving this inventory?
questions.description: Identify the reason — insurance documentation, moving out, estate planning, rental handover, or general record-keeping — as it shapes what must be captured.

questions.title: Is there a deadline this needs to be completed by?
questions.description: Establish whether there is a fixed date (policy renewal, moving day, etc.) that constrains when and how quickly the task must be done.

questions.title: What device or app will you use to take photos?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user will use a smartphone, a dedicated camera, or a home inventory app, as this affects workflow and file organization.

questions.title: What format should the final record be delivered in?
questions.description: Determine whether the output should be a photo album, a labeled spreadsheet, a PDF report, a cloud folder, or an insurance portal upload.

questions.title: Should items be documented with values or serial numbers too?
questions.description: Find out whether photos alone suffice or if item descriptions, estimated values, purchase receipts, and serial numbers should also be captured per item.
